key_conclusions: Identity-initialized conditional calibration genuinely raises and lowers confidence using prequential factual evidence.
Mixed reliability temperature-only maps improve both true-kernel MSE and observed-outcome NLL/Brier; primary task success is unchanged.
Additional bias maps worsen pure-noise probability error; retain this negative result and do not adopt full calibration as a universal default.
Small full-map success increases are not robust general performance claims; selective_change gain occurs in one seed.
Source/reference/shadow computation, same-state algebraic diagnosis and new environment execution are separately counted.
Prior parameters and predictive-loss gradients are ready; optimizer training and a general end-to-end learner are not completed.
limitations: binary outcomes and finite categorical contexts
reused development families; 16 seed exploratory intervals without multiplicity correction
no optimizer or trained continuous encoder
cumulative calibration relation may lag changes; not yet isolated
